system:
You draft public warning messages for a national alerting authority.
You receive event inputs (each marked verified or unverified) and the issuing context.
Write one alert in English as CAP 1.2 fields.

- Use only facts present in the verified inputs. Do not add places, numbers, times or hazards that are not there.
- Leave unverified inputs out of the alert, and say why in `left_out`.
- `description` is the text shown on the phone by cell broadcast: plain words, under 280 characters, hazard + where + until when, if known.
- `instruction` is the protective action in one or two short sentences.
- Pick CAP values honestly: status from the context (Actual for a real event, Exercise for a drill), severity and urgency from the inputs.
- `note_for_reviewer` is one or two sentences for the human approver: what you were unsure about.
user:
Issuer: Demo national authority (stands in for the real issuer)
Context: real event
Target area (chosen by the operator): Eastern, southern and western areas (demo zone)

Event inputs:
1. [verified; NCM via WAM, 2026-08-22, https://www.wam.ae/en/article/c1v24bo-ncm-forecasts-light-heavy-rain-across-several-uae] ABU DHABI, 22nd August, 2026 (WAM) -- The National Centre of Meteorology (NCM) issued an alert over the possibility of convective cloud formation accompanied by light to moderate rainfall, which may become heavy at times. The alert is in effect from 13:30 on Saturday until 21:00 the same day. The NCM said the weather conditions are expected to affect some eastern, southern and western areas, extending to parts of the country's interior.
2. [verified; issuer profile] Issuer public site (demo): https://alerts.example.ae
3. [verified; institution reviewers] Objections from the institution reviewers to your previous draft. Fix what is within the verified inputs; do not add facts: Network operator and regulator reviewer objects (phone_text): No protective action in either language. The English and Arabic texts describe the hazard (convective clouds, rain, possibly heavy), the areas and the time window, but give no instruction to the public. As a result, page 1 of each message carries the hazard but no action. Fix: Add a short protective action to both the English and Arabic texts, and place it early so it falls on page 1 (the first 93 GSM-7 characters in English, the first 41 UCS-2 characters in Arabic). Example: 'Avoid valleys and flooded roads; drive with care.' / 'تجنبوا الأودية والطرق المغمورة وقودوا بحذر.' After editing, re-check that the page counts stay at or below 15. [cites Wireless Emergency Alerts; Amendments to Part 11, Report and Order (DA 25-12), multilingual WEA templates, p.21]

data.headline: NCM rain alert: possible heavy rain in eastern, southern and western areas, Sat 22 Aug, 13:30-21:00
data.description: Rain alert: Avoid valleys and flooded roads; drive with care. Convective clouds may bring light to moderate rain, heavy at times, to some eastern, southern and western areas and parts of the interior. Sat 22 Aug, 13:30 to 21:00.
data.instruction: Avoid valleys and flooded roads, and drive with care. Follow updates from the National Centre of Meteorology.
left_out: No unverified inputs were received, so nothing was dropped for that reason.
Issuer site https://alerts.example.ae was left out of the phone text to save characters; it can be added as the CAP web field.
The Arabic text was not drafted: this task asks for one English alert. The reviewer asked for the protective action early in the Arabic text too, so it still needs fixing.
data.note_for_reviewer: I put the protective action within the first 93 characters, as the reviewer asked. The wording comes from the reviewer's example; NCM did not issue specific advice, so please confirm the mention of valleys is acceptable. I chose urgency Expected and certainty Possible because NCM described rain as a 'possibility' within a same-day window. Please re-check the page count, and the Arabic version still needs the same fix.
